summary: Okanogan County, WA: 1934 L-4 cab on Buttermilk Butte, sold and moved to a private ranch up the Twisp River in 1951; the association lists a standing cab at Reynaud.

facts.status_note: The cab was sold and moved to a private ranch in 1951; the association lists the original site as gone

access.note: The cab went to a private ranch in 1951; no source describes public access to the summit or the ranch

corrections.current: The lookout was moved to Reynaud.
corrections.proposed: Sold to a private party in 1951 and moved to a ranch 4 miles up the Twisp River; the association lists a standing cab at Reynaud, a link the sources do not explain
corrections.why: The register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb place the cab on a ranch up the Twisp River; Reynaud appears only as the association's label for the standing cab

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 1934, but WillhiteWeb says the September 1934 panoramas show no evidence of a structure. The story keeps 1934 as the register's date and reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Register and FireLookout.com agree on the 1934 cab and the 1951 sale and move. The Reynaud link is unconfirmed: the association gives the standing cab that name, while the register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb say a ranch 4 miles up the Twisp River. A WebSearch snippet of a 2021 Methow Valley News item (https://methowvalleynews.com/2021/07/14/valley-life-twisp-20/) describes a 1951 public-auction sale to a Reynaud family member. It is not cited: fetch_text returned no readable text from the cached copy (gzip-compressed), so no quote could be checked. Re-read it if fetch_text is fixed to decompress. The summit's current condition is not described anywhere we read. No new photos added.
